summary: We developed an interactive game that allows participants to experience the process of designing and managing a space mission in a practical way. The project addresses the challenge of solving the current limitation of learning, which is usually purely theoretical or fragmented across isolated tools. This project is important because it connects theory with real-time strategic decision-making, allowing participants to experience how each technical choice affects the complete destiny of an expedition, fostering critical thinking and complex problem-solving. details:
This game is situated in the year 2085, in a context where Earth is going through a natural resource crisis, which forces players to organize an expedition to the newly discovered planet “Kepler-22b” to collect vital information, check for the presence of life, and return safely. The game allows participation individually or in cooperative multiplayer mode (up to 2 players), allowing them to assume specific roles: Mission commander, Aerospace engineer, planetary scientist and Medic ans survival specialist. The experience is divided into five sequential stages: designing the ship (build a resistant ship without spending the entire budget), preparing the crew (choose a balanced crew to face unforeseen events), space trip (decide how to solve each emergency using available resources), planet exploration (investigate the soil, water, atmosphere, and possible signs of life without endangering the crew) and Earth returning (complete the mission and bring back the research results). Upon conclusion, an evaluation system wards up to 1.000 points according to the milestones reached (arriving the planet, keeping the team safe, completing research, returning and conserving resources), classifying the mission as successful (800 - 1.000), partially successful (500 - 799) or failed (0 - 499).

The main innovative value of our project consists of integrating, into a unique interactive experience, the strategic planification, resources management and optimization, space exploration and scientific-problem solving. Unlike traditional methods, our videogame turns the gamer into a main character of a mission where each decision has real consequences, offering the benefit of learning from both successes and failures. By this way, combination of 3D simulation, progressive challenges and cooperation between players allows to develop critical thinking and different scientific abilities in a dynamic, accessible and entertaining way. Additionally, by having a bilingual system in Spanish and English, it opens up universal players around the world. Given all this, the anticipated impact of our project is based on awakening the interest in space exploration and technological careers in students and youth, connecting complex engineering concepts with an interactive and motivating narrative.

For the development of the interactive environment, we initially used “Opencode” (a tool recommended by our teacher Marisa Quiroga), with which we created the first prototype, establishing the structure, functions, and basic mechanics of the game. Then, we used “Claude”, at the suggestion of the software engineer and event mentor Sabrina Ojeda, to perfect the previous design by incorporating animations, sound, difficulty levels, a progress bar, and various graphic resources.

During the development of the project, we investigated Kepler-22b —a real exoplanet discovered by the Kepler mission of NASA, located approximately 600 light-years from Earth and situated in a habitable zone of its star— to achieve an accurate representation. Although its surface conditions and the existence of life haven’t been confirmed yet, we used this framework as a starting point to develop a futuristic simulation that combines real scientific data with hypothetical scenarios. On the other hand, incorporating the valuable suggestions offered by our mentors throughout the day, and despite being a simulation, we applied our creativity to design an animated environment that blends the technical elements of the mission with details characteristic of our educational institution and our country.
